body: Basically we want to share a custom ESLint config between 10-20 repos where the custom config extends **eslint-config-node-style-guide**, but we don't want to have to install the **eslint-config-node-style-guide** module as a dependency in each of those projects. Ideally we'd just be able to bundle the eslint-config-node-style-guide dependency in our custom config and only need to install **eslint** and **eslint-config-extends-test**.

repository.name: eslint-config-gulp
repository.description: Sharable eslint config for gulp projects

body: We can make a (breaking) change to update where extends is calculated from, but I'd still encourage you to use the method I described. That lets you be in complete control of his rules are change and merged, and also makes debugging easier.

@nzakas i think it's not "nice" to put data (your rules) into some other modules (base). also it wouldn't work if _base_ would use _extends_ (eg [airbnb](https://github.com/airbnb/javascript/blob/170dbeb5d45e2fb226efdad9f04bd939e6756393/packages/eslint-config-airbnb/base.js)) without installing it into your project rather than into _eslint-config-extends-test_.

+1 for a fix of this bug
@t128 you can always clone the object and modify that if you want to be "nice".

@nzakas Actually, your solution works with simple modules such as **eslint-config-node-style-guide** which is basically a single JSON file of rules.
But I just tried converting one of our other projects and it broke since **eslint-config-airbnb** uses a complex web of nested extends and rules files.

In my **eslint-config-blah** custom rules module, I extend **airbnb/base** using the following:

``` js
var base = require('eslint-config-airbnb/base');

base.extends.unshift('eslint:recommended');

base.rules['comma-dangle'] = [2, 'never'];
base.rules['indent'] = [2, 2, {'SwitchCase': 1}];
base.rules['no-console'] = 1;
base.rules['no-use-before-define'] = [2, 'nofunc'];

module.exports = base;
```

Which seems to correctly output the following config:

``` js
{ extends:
   [ 'eslint:recommended',
     'eslint-config-airbnb/legacy',
     'eslint-config-airbnb/rules/es6' ],
  parser: 'babel-eslint',
  rules:
   { 'comma-dangle': [ 2, 'never' ],
     indent: [ 2, 2, [Object] ],
     'no-console': 1,
     'no-use-before-define': [ 2, 'nofunc' ] } }
```

But when I try and run my `$ gulp lint` task, I get the following error because it can no longer resolve those **eslint-config-airbnb** references since they were specified as a dependency in my **eslint-config-blah** module, and not declared as a dependency of my main project:


So it looks like if my custom ESLint config extends **eslint-config-airbnb** style guide, I'll need to include that dependency in each of my projects as well, and can't hide that as an implementation detail in my module.
